name: gardner in rounds against the chase
description: Martin Gardner's 5x5 minichess played in rounds: both players move at once. Each round each player chooses one move in secret, and both moves are revealed and made together. There is no check: the king is simply captured, and the side that loses its king loses. Only two pieces moving onto the same square collide, and then both are removed. Two pieces that try to take each other in the same round meet half-way as a collision and both are removed, kings included, so striking back at an attacker that strikes is mutual destruction. A piece that moves onto a square its target has just left for somewhere else lands there if it could move to an empty square; a pawn's diagonal capture, which cannot land on an empty square, misses and the pawn stays. The piece that made a player's move rests: it may not make that player's move in the next round, unless it is the only piece that can move. So a king cannot run two rounds running and no piece can strike twice in a row: every attack gives a round's warning, and a king that has just run must have run to a square no standing enemy piece can reach. If both kings fall in the same round, the side with more material left wins (queen 9, rook 5, bishop and knight 3, pawn 1) and equal material is a draw; the same count settles a game that reaches the move limit or the no-progress clock. A round counts as two moves on the clocks. In play the chase is gone: a king may not run two rounds running, so attacks are answered once and most games are won by striking a king that had just moved and so had to stand.

provenance.history: S4, the candidate game: Gardner in rounds with all three of schema 27's switches against the royal chase (rest, swap collision, both score) and rules.scoring material. Pre-registered in docs/plan-round-chase.md section 5 before it was measured; the study and its grades are there. Joined the library from preview by Q934 (2026-10-17): the library's first royal game played in rounds, Gardner's board and army played in rounds rather than by turns and made decisive (0.971 of games) by the three switches together; viable 4-0 at 0.514. The rest alone (gardner in rounds resting) stays a preview beside it, as the contrast.
